d_sv_content.name: Combination of Lapatinib and Fractionated Radiation Therapy for Dogs with Transitional Cell Carcinoma
d_sv_content.tagline: Help us study canine bladder translational cell carcinoma.
d_sv_content.description: This study is for dogs that have bladder cancer called transitional cell carcinoma (TCC). The goal is to find out if using radiation therapy together with a pill called lapatinib is safe and well‑tolerated by dogs. Researchers will watch closely for side effects and see how dogs respond to the treatment over about 4 months.
d_sv_content.requirements: Daily oral lapatinib and a non‑steroidal anti‑inflammatory drug (NSAID) throughout the study15 daily radiation treatments, which require anesthesia each time, within the first 7 days of starting the pillsMonthly recheck visits for 3 months after radiation for exams and blood testsUrinary ultrasounds to measure the tumor before the study starts and at the endAll study visits must take place at Colorado State University (CSU) Veterinary Health Systems facilities (VHS)
d_sv_content.responsibilities: Pay for the initial exam and all tests needed to diagnose the bladder tumor (including bladder scope and biopsy)Pay for the NSAID medication during the studyBring your dog to all scheduled appointmentsGive your dog oral medications every dayKeep a written log of medications and any side effects you notice
d_sv_content.whoCan: Dogs may be able to join if they:Have a biopsy‑confirmed diagnosis of bladder TCCCan safely receive an NSAIDAre healthy enough to undergo daily anesthesia for radiation treatmentHave not had radiation in the last 6 weeks or chemotherapy in the last 2 weeksCan come to CSU VHS facilities for all study visits
d_sv_content.benefits: BenefitsHigh quality care for your petThe study covers the cost of:LapatinibRecheck examsBloodwork during the study$3,000 toward radiation therapy, which is provided at a reduced costUrinary ultrasounds at the beginning and end of the studySedation for ultrasounds if neededSome funds are available to help pay for treatment of side effects caused by the studyRisksPossible side effects from radiation therapy, lapatinib, or NSAIDsRisks related to repeated anesthesiaThe treatment may or may not help your dog’s cancer
d_sv_content.compensation:
The study covers the cost of: Lapatinib, recheck exams, bloodwork during the study, $3,000 toward radiation therapy, urinary ultrasounds at the beginning and end of the study, sedation for ultrasounds if needed.
Some funds are available to help pay for treatment of side effects caused by the study.
d_sv_content.timeCommitment:
Study course: 4 months.
15 consecutive days of radiation therapy within the first 7 days of starting study drugs. Monthly rechecks for 3 months after finishing radiation therapy. Study drugs daily over the entire 4-month course of the study.
